incidents.victim: German university hospitals (Cologne, Freiburg, Heidelberg, Tübingen, Ulm, Mannheim) via Unimed billing provider
incidents.vector: Compromise of Unimed, a third-party billing service provider used by German university hospitals; attackers exfiltrated patient and billing records starting in mid-April.
incidents.impact: Nearly 30,000 patients affected at Cologne, 54,000 at Freiburg, 11,000 at Heidelberg, plus thousands more at Ulm, Tübingen and Mannheim; stolen data includes names, addresses, treating physicians, and in hundreds of cases health and diagnosis information; hospitals halted data transfers, filed criminal complaints and are weighing legal action.

incidents.victim: Multiple sectors in US, Israel, UAE and Middle East (tech, aerospace, defense, telecom)
incidents.vector: Iran-nexus APT (tracked as Screening Serpens / UNC1549) used tailored fake job recruitment lures and DLL sideloading with AppDomainManager hijacking to deploy new MiniUpdate and MiniJunk V2 remote access trojans from February through April 2026.
incidents.impact: Six new RAT variants observed against entities in the US, Israel, UAE and two additional Middle Eastern targets; campaign tempo aligned with the regional conflict that started Feb. 28, 2026; Unit 42 assesses moderate-high confidence attribution and notes continuous development of upgraded variants.

incidents.vector: CISA contractor with admin access to the agency's development platform created a public GitHub repository ("Private-CISA") and disabled GitHub's built-in secret-publishing protections, exposing AWS GovCloud admin credentials, an RSA private key for a CISA-IT GitHub app, plaintext passwords for dozens of internal systems and other sensitive build/deploy artifacts.
incidents.impact: GitGuardian and TruffleHog researchers say it is one of the worst government data leaks in recent memory; more than a week after notification CISA was still rotating keys and had not invalidated a private key granting full repo, CI/CD and admin access to CISA-IT GitHub; Sens. Hassan and Rep. Thompson demanding answers; no confirmed downstream compromise yet but adversary exploitation window is wide open.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — service provider to ransomware and fraud actors
incidents.vector: Europol-led operation by French and Dutch authorities, with support from eight additional countries, dismantled 33 servers, seized multiple domains (including 1vpns.com/.net/.org) and arrested the alleged administrator at a residence in Ukraine.
incidents.impact: First VPN, marketed on Russian-speaking cybercrime forums and tied to most major Europol-supported cybercrime investigations, was taken offline; investigators obtained the user database and identified thousands of users tied to ransomware and fraud, feeding 21 additional inquiries globally; affected users were notified that their identities are now known to law enforcement.

incidents.victim: US federal civilian agencies and downstream enterprises (Trend Micro Apex One and Langflow users)
incidents.vector: CISA added CVE-2025-34291 (Langflow Origin Validation Error) and CVE-2026-34926 (Trend Micro Apex One on-prem directory traversal) to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog based on evidence of active in-the-wild exploitation.
incidents.impact: Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies must remediate by the due date under BOD 22-01; CISA urged all organizations to prioritize patching as the bugs are being actively used against enterprise security and AI/ML application servers.

incidents.vector: NYDFS issued an industry letter warning that frontier AI models and geopolitical events have produced a heightened cybersecurity threat environment, and laid out non-mandatory but expected additional controls (phishing-resistant MFA, KEV-driven patching, secure programming, backup testing, third-party validation).
incidents.impact: Regulated banks, insurers and fintechs are expected to layer additional defensive measures on top of 23 NYCRR Part 500; the unusual public guidance signals NYDFS sees current threat level (driven in part by AI-accelerated vulnerability discovery and exploitation) as a near-term risk to financial sector operations.

incidents.vector: TeamPCP (a suspected North Korean group also behind recent npm/PyPI supply-chain attacks) compromised a GitHub employee's device via a poisoned Visual Studio Code extension and exfiltrated internal source code repositories.
incidents.impact: GitHub confirmed roughly 3,800 internal repositories were taken; the company says customer data was unaffected, the malicious extension was removed, the endpoint isolated and high-priority secrets rotated the same day; TeamPCP advertised the code for sale at $50,000 on a cybercrime forum and threatened to release it for free if no buyer emerged.

incidents.vector: ShinyHunters accessed a 7-Eleven system used to store franchisee documents, part of a broader campaign against Salesforce-hosted data stores at numerous companies in late April.
incidents.impact: 7-Eleven confirmed the breach to regulators in Maine, Vermont and Massachusetts; stolen data includes names, addresses and Social Security numbers from franchisee records; comes alongside ShinyHunters' Instructure/Canvas breach against US universities and K-12 schools, which prompted an FBI 'do not pay' advisory.

incidents.victim: npm ecosystem (@antv packages, echarts-for-react, ~169 downstream packages) and their CI/CD users
incidents.vector: TeamPCP compromised an @antv maintainer account and published malicious versions of widely used data-visualization packages; the obfuscated preinstall payload (Mini Shai-Hulud) runs during npm install on GitHub Actions Linux runners, scrapes Runner.Worker process memory and steals credentials for GitHub, AWS, HashiCorp Vault, npm, Kubernetes and 1Password.
incidents.impact: Malicious versions propagated through echarts-for-react (1M+ weekly downloads) into thousands of downstream projects; GitHub removed 640 malicious packages and invalidated 61,274 npm granular tokens with write/2FA-bypass permissions; payload forges SLSA provenance via Sigstore, creates rogue public repos under victim accounts (>2,200 observed) and establishes persistent credential capture in CI/CD pipelines.

incidents.victim: KimWolf DDoS botnet operator / DoD and other US victims of the botnet
incidents.vector: Ontario Provincial Police arrested 23-year-old Ottawa resident Jacob Butler (aka 'Dort') on a US extradition warrant for operating KimWolf, an IoT botnet of more than one million infected residential proxy devices (digital photo frames, web cameras, streaming boxes) used for DDoS-for-hire.
incidents.impact: KimWolf was tied to record-breaking DDoS attacks measured near 30 Tbps, more than 25,000 attack commands and victim losses exceeding $1 million in some cases; the botnet also targeted US Department of Defense IP ranges, prompting DCIS and FBI investigation; infrastructure for KimWolf and three rival botnets (Aisuru, JackSkid, Mossad) had already been seized in March, and Butler now faces up to 10 years in US prison plus Canadian computer-misuse charges.

incidents.victim: High-profile individuals in Japan, Taiwan and South Korea (Chinese-speaking diaspora, technical and government targets)
incidents.vector: Tropic Trooper (aka Pirate Panda / Earth Centaur) compromised victims' home Wi-Fi routers to perform DNS hijacking of a Chinese dictionary app's update server, then delivered a Cobalt Strike beacon and new malware families (DaveShell, Donut loader, Merlin/Apollo agents, C6DOOR) via trojanized installers; secondary campaigns used Signal-impersonation phishing pages and military-themed lures.
incidents.impact: Itochu and Zscaler researchers presented at Black Hat Asia that the long-running Chinese APT has shifted to targeting personal devices outside corporate networks, expanded its victim set into Japan, Taiwan and South Korea, and is rapidly adopting open-source loaders and C2 frameworks; IoCs for the campaign were published for defenders in the region.
